issues.detail: Installation steps and commands are Debian/Ubuntu-centric (apt, systemctl, sudo) and RHEL, FreeBSD and Windows are only mentioned in passing without commands, despite the compatibility claim.

scenarios.name: ssh-brute-force-ban-ubuntu
scenarios.rationale: Both install the engine plus nftables bouncer, install the sshd collection, reload via systemctl, and use cscli explain with --type syslog plus cscli decisions list; A adds a burst test, journald fallback, and bouncer verification, while B is more concise but also correct and covers the rubric items fully.

scenarios.name: remote-bouncer-allowlist-manual-ban
scenarios.rationale: Both cover all four rubric items (bouncer key, YAML api_url/api_key, allowlist create/add, 24h ban, bouncers list verification), but A is more complete and runnable, with LAPI listen_uri, a firewall rule and a fallback for older versions, while B leaves the listen_uri setting to the docs and refers to a 'reference' the user never saw.
